content.user_title: Analyze Mass Spectrometry Data with PyOpenMS
content.value_statement: Mass spectrometry workflows require precise file handling, signal processing, and identification steps. This skill guides PyOpenMS workflows for proteomics, metabolomics, feature detection, and quantification.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading and writing mzML, idXML, featureXML, consensusXML, FASTA, mzTab, and related OpenMS formats.
Explains PyOpenMS data structures such as MSExperiment, MSSpectrum, FeatureMap, ConsensusMap, and identification objects.
Provides examples for smoothing, filtering, centroiding, peak picking, and feature detection workflows.
Documents peptide and protein identification workflows with FDR filtering, protein inference, and search parameters.
Covers metabolomics preprocessing, feature annotation, normalization, blank filtering, missing value imputation, and table export.
limitations: Does not execute analyses, install packages, or validate local data automatically.
Requires valid mass spectrometry files, search results, and installed PyOpenMS dependencies.
Examples may need adaptation for instrument settings, file sizes, and search engine availability.
Does not replace statistical review, database curation, or domain-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Proteomics Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan peptide identification, FDR filtering, protein inference, and result export with PyOpenMS objects.

use_cases.title: Process LC-MS Data
use_cases.description: Design file loading, smoothing, centroiding, feature detection, alignment, and consensus feature workflows.

use_cases.title: Build Metabolomics Tables
use_cases.description: Structure feature annotation, normalization, blank filtering, missing value handling, and analysis table export.

prompt_templates.title: Load a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to load an mzML file with PyOpenMS and inspect spectra, chromatograms, retention times, and peak counts.

prompt_templates.title: Detect Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a PyOpenMS feature detection workflow for centroided LC-MS data, including key parameters and output files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Identifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through peptide and protein identification review, FDR filtering, q-value handling, and protein inference in PyOpenMS.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PyOpenMS LC-MS/MS pipeline plan from raw files through feature detection, alignment, annotation, quantification, and exports.

output_examples.input: I need to compare feature intensities across several LC-MS samples.
output: Load each feature map and align retention times before grouping features.
Create a consensus map so each row represents a shared feature across samples.
Export the consensus data to a table for quality control and statistical analysis.

output_examples.input: I have peptide identification results and need to control false discoveries.
output: Load protein and peptide identifications from idXML or mzIdentML files.
Apply false discovery rate filtering and keep hits below the selected q-value threshold.
Run protein inference after peptide filtering so reported proteins reflect accepted evidence.

output_examples.input: I want to prepare metabolomics data for downstream statistics.
output: Annotate features with mass tolerance checks against a curated compound database.
Normalize intensities, remove blank-driven features, and handle missing values consistently.
Export an analysis-ready table with m/z, retention time, feature identifiers, and sample intensities.

best_practices: Confirm file formats and centroiding state before selecting PyOpenMS algorithms.
Record key parameters such as tolerances, enzymes, modifications, and FDR thresholds.
Validate exported tables with quality control plots and domain-specific review.
anti_patterns: Do not run default feature detection parameters without checking instrument resolution and data type.
Do not compare raw intensities across samples before alignment, grouping, and normalization.
Do not report protein or metabolite calls without database provenance and uncertainty checks.

faq.question: What is PyOpenMS used for?
faq.answer: PyOpenMS provides Python access to OpenMS algorithms for computational mass spectrometry, proteomics, metabolomics, and LC-MS/MS workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run PyOpenMS for me?
faq.answer: No. It guides workflow design and code patterns, but execution depends on your local environment and data.

faq.question: Which file formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers formats such as mzML, mzXML, idXML, mzIdentML, featureXML, consensusXML, FASTA, pepXML, protXML, and mzTab.

faq.question: Can it help with peptide identification?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains loading identification files, applying FDR filtering, reviewing hits, and performing protein inference.

faq.question: Can it support metabolomics workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers feature detection, annotation, normalization, blank filtering, missing value handling, and table export.

faq.question: What should I provide in prompts?
faq.answer: Provide file formats, instrument type, acquisition mode, analysis goal, search engine details, and any required thresholds.
